what.text: A user story describes a feature from the end user's point of view. It's the agile way to capture requirements: a sentence or two, plus a conversation.

template.text: The common template: as a role, I want a capability, so that I get a benefit.

ex.text: As a passenger, I want to link my credit card to my profile, so that I can pay for a ride faster.

backlog.text: Stories live in the backlog, an ordered list, often on index cards or sticky notes.

tree.text: Big goals break down. An initiative holds epics. An epic is a large body of work, delivered over several sprints. It breaks into stories, small enough for a one or two week sprint.

i.text: Independent: build them in any order.

v.text: Valuable: each one delivers value to users.

accept.text: Acceptance criteria tell the team when a story is done. Ensure the bidder can log in, reach the auction page, and select a product.
